what: the OpenFold3 gradient defect, localised to ONE leaf, from device_gradient_043pt.json's per-tensor array (547 tensors: rel_l2, norm_ratio, cos, ref_norm, device_norm) cross-referenced against the per-tensor reference mass. No new run -- both artifacts already existed on qb2 and had never been read together.
headline: 24 tensors -- one leaf, diffusion_transformer.blocks.N.attention_pair_bias.layer_norm_a.layer_norm_s.weight -- are 25.5795 % of the model's squared gradient norm and read mass-weighted rel_l2 10.6980 with norm ratio 7.8658. The other 523 compared tensors, holding almost exactly the same mass (25.5563 %), read 0.2929. Strip that one leaf and the arm's mass-weighted rel falls from 7.5692 to 0.2929.

the_control_that_came_free.claim: there are TWO instances of tenstorrent.AdaLN per DiT block, built from the same class with the same code and driven with the same (a, s). One fails 59x worse than the other.
the_control_that_came_free.what_it_settles: a defect in the AdaLN class's backward -- including the sigmoid-gated multiply, which pass 152 called the last surviving candidate -- would hit BOTH instances. It hits one. The class is exonerated by the model's own natural A/B and the defect is in what the block does around adaln_a.

whole compared set.note: the mass-weighted figure is 45.6x the median the campaign has been quoting. PROTOCOL A23's argument, at the largest scale available.

magnitude_or_direction.reading: dominantly MAGNITUDE -- our diffusion gradient is ~4.4x too large by mass, ~5.2x across the twenty heaviest tensors -- with a substantial direction component on 15.03 % of the model and outright anti-correlation on 4.81 %.

the_worst_tensor_in_full.reading: 19.24x too large AND 41 degrees off. Not precision.

per_block_reading: not a gradient of severity -- qualitative. norm_ratio runs 0.71 to 19.24 and cos runs -0.80 to +0.998, with FOUR blocks anti-correlated (0: -0.796, 3: -0.169, 6: -0.805, 7: -0.014) and nine above 0.97 with r near unity. Some blocks are fine and some have gradients pointing the wrong way, in the same leaf.
d53_hypothesis_REFUTED: D53 filed, as an explicitly open hypothesis with its own falsification condition, that rel rises with mass inside this family. Over all 24 blocks the log-log slope is 0.1657 with Pearson 0.3067. REFUTED. The six points that suggested it were the six worst of 24 -- a selected tail, exactly the failure mode D53 predicted for itself.
leads_not_findings: layer_norm_a.linear_s.weight reads mass-weighted norm ratio 1.0980 while linear_g reads ~5 and the gain 7.87. In AdaLN, out = a_norm * sigmoid(s_scale) + s_bias, so d/d s_bias = g_out directly while d/d s_scale = g_out * a_norm * sigmoid'. linear_s being near-right says the cotangent ARRIVING at the AdaLN output is essentially correct, and the error is in the a_norm * sigmoid' factor -- or in a_norm itself, which the tape RECOMPUTES in the backward rather than retaining.

a_ln is consumed twice on the attention side (the fused padded QKV projection at openfold3_diffusion_transformer.py:189, head_dim 48 -> 64, and the query gate at :218), and that path also carries nlp_create_qkv_heads and the slice o[:, :, :, :HEAD_DIM] that drops the 16 padding channels. a_t is consumed twice too, so multiple consumption is not the difference -- but the padded head dim and the slice that undoes it exist ONLY on the failing side. A backward that does not zero the padding region would inject structure rather than noise, vary per block, and produce negative cosines.
these are leads. Nothing here measures either of them.
what_this_does_not_establish: it does not name the defect, and it does not say the 523 other tensors are acceptable -- at mass-weighted 0.2929 they are still 14.6x the 2.0e-02 bar, and only 2.7940 % of the model is inside the 5.0e-02 per-tensor bar. It says where 25.5795 % of the model's gradient goes wrong and that the AdaLN class itself is not the cause. One batch, one r = 0 step, one crop.
